main.title: 호남 반도체 시대 열리나…삼성·SK 2000조 쏟아붓는다
main.body: Samsung and SK will publicly announce massive investment plans on June 29, centered on establishing a semiconductor cluster in the Honam region. The combined investment is projected to reach nearly 2,000 trillion won over ten years. Samsung Electronics plans to construct 4-5 semiconductor fabrication plants on the former Gwangju military airport site. SK Hynix will similarly build 4-5 fabrication plants in the Gwangju area. Beyond semiconductors, Samsung Display will invest approximately 100 trillion won in OLED production at its Asan and Cheonan campuses. Additional investments include packaging facilities in Cheonan and Onyang by Samsung, and increased NAND flash production at SK Hynix's Cheongju facility. SK Group plans to establish gigawatt-scale AI data centers across five nationwide locations. Industry observers raise feasibility questions, citing concentrated semiconductor ecosystem resources in Seoul metropolitan areas and infrastructure challenges regarding water supply and power availability in Honam. Park Jaehyun, research fellow at KAIST, cautions that semiconductor cluster success depends heavily on dense supplier networks and skilled workforce availability—conditions that may be difficult to replicate outside the existing metropolitan semiconductor belt.
main.keep_reason: Korean primary on 2,000조 mega-investment with specific fab counts (Samsung 4-5, SK 4-5 in Gwangju), Display OLED 100조, SK 5개 GW AI DC — most operationally detailed Korean source.
main.select_reason: 윈도우 최대 사건 — Samsung 4-5팹 + SK 4-5팹 + Display 100조 + 5GW급 AI DC 5개소까지 운영 수치가 가장 구체적인 한국어 1차 보도, 메인 헤드라인.

main.title: Samsung, SK reportedly to invest $1.3 trillion over 10 years
main.body: South Korea's Samsung Group and SK Group plan to announce approximately 2,000 trillion won ($1.3 trillion) in investments over the next decade as part of President Lee Jae Myung's industrial strategy, according to Korea Economic Daily reporting. The two conglomerates are expected to present their investment plans during a presidential office meeting. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix each plan to construct four to five semiconductor fabrication plants in the Gwangju area. Additionally, Samsung will establish chip packaging facilities in South Chungcheong province, while SK Hynix will expand NAND plants in North Chungcheong province. President Lee will unveil the Three Mega Projects for the Great Leap Forward initiative at a 2 p.m. event. Officials from industry, science, climate, and land ministries will present government policy measures before the companies reveal their investment commitments. The combined investment commitment of 2,000 trillion won exceeds an earlier report indicating Samsung alone would announce over 1,000 trillion won in spending. Presidential policy chief Kim Yong-beom indicated that very unusual figures would be unveiled, with plans focusing on semiconductors, AI data centers, and physical AI development.
main.keep_reason: Samsung+SK 2,000조원($1.3T) 10-year semi+AI DC mega-investment under President Lee's Three Mega Projects — defining strategic projects beat for the window (English primary with $ framing).
main.select_reason: id 16과 같은 사건의 영어 1차($1.3조 framing) — 글로벌/달러 표기 컨텍스트 보완용으로 한국어 1차와 함께 keep (한국어+영문 1차 보완 예외).

main.title: Why Wall Street thinks US memory maker Micron is the next Nvidia
main.body: Micron, based in Boise, Idaho, has become a Wall Street favorite among memory chip manufacturers. The company briefly surpassed Meta and Tesla in market valuation on Thursday, closing Friday with approximately $1.27 trillion in market cap. Its stock has surged over 236% in the past month alone, reaching $1,132 per share. The surge stems from the AI infrastructure boom creating severe shortages of system memory chips, including DRAM, NAND, and High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM). AI servers require significantly more memory than traditional devices. Major buyers—Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon AWS, Google, Meta, and Oracle—are purchasing enormous quantities, forcing other manufacturers like Dell and HP to hoard supplies. This shortage, termed RAMageddon, is expected to persist through 2027, already driving up consumer electronics prices for Apple products and gaming consoles. Micron delivered exceptional third-quarter earnings: revenue quadrupled year-over-year to $41.45 billion, while profits skyrocketed from $1.88 billion to $28.2 billion. The company forecasted fourth-quarter revenue between $49-51 billion. To address historical industry cycles where demand collapses when capacity increases, Micron signed 16 long-term strategic customer agreements across data center, consumer, and automotive segments. Analysts believe these contracts could create sustainable earnings growth and protect against market downturns.
main.keep_reason: RAMageddon HBM/DRAM/NAND shortage through 2027 with Q3 revenue 4x to $41.45B, 16 long-term contracts — core AI infra supply constraint signal for DPU/memory ecosystem.
main.select_reason: Micron 시가총액 1.27조 달러로 Meta·Tesla 초월, Q3 매출 4배·이익 15배 — RAMageddon이 2027년까지 지속되는 메모리 공급 충격은 DPU/HBM/AI 인프라 전반의 비용 곡선과 직결, Samsung/SK와 독립된 두 번째 헤드라인.

main.title: '미소스 5' 미국 내 제한적 배포 허용…'페이블 5'는 금지 유지
main.body: The U.S. government has granted limited access to Anthropic's Misos 5 model to select American organizations, while maintaining restrictions on the public-facing Fable 5 model. According to Reuters, Anthropic received notification from the government that it could redistribute Misos 5 to trusted U.S. institutions and companies managing critical infrastructure—approximately 100 organizations, including Fortune 500 companies and infrastructure operators participating in Project Glasswing. Commerce Secretary Howard Rutnik's letter clarified that approved companies and their employees need no separate export licenses for Misos 5, even if non-U.S. citizens. However, unlisted companies face continued restrictions, with access limited to domestic organizations only. Anthropic expanded Misos Preview distribution to about 150 global institutions on June 2nd, though Fable 5 remains unavailable to the general public. Misos 5 and Fable 5 share the same base model, but Misos 5 removes certain safeguards for security and defense purposes. The selective authorization has drawn criticism from the AI industry and civil rights groups for lacking transparency regarding selection criteria. FIRE legislative advisor John Coleman noted: We cannot know how these companies were selected or why others were excluded, calling it excessive government power. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman similarly questioned whether government should directly choose AI companies' customers. Experts warn excessive government control may undermine U.S. AI competitiveness, potentially allowing China to narrow technological gaps.
main.keep_reason: US government limited Misos 5 release to ~100 critical-infra orgs (Project Glasswing) — sovereign-AI export-control framework now operational, shapes global AI access landscape.
main.select_reason: Project Glasswing ~100개 조직 한정 배포, Rutnik 상무장관 서한, Altman/FIRE 비판 — 정부 주도 sovereign AI 거버넌스가 본격 가동된 첫 케이스, 한국 시장도 직접적 파급.

main.title: 김준기 래블업 CTO "풀스택 AI 인프라로 GPU 한계 넘는다"
main.body: The South Korean AI market has seen a surge in services emphasizing stable and efficient GPU supply. As GPU prices rise and inference demand expands, companies face increasing AI infrastructure complexity alongside diverse hardware options like energy-efficient NPUs. Founded in 2015, Rablup (CEO Shin Jung-gyul) is shifting focus from model development and pretraining toward inference and agent services. Backend.AI serves as their core platform—orchestrating heterogeneous GPU and NPU clusters across hyperscale multitenant environments. Kim Jun-gi, Rablup's CTO, explains: Most companies now prioritize inference and operational readiness from the start. Backend.AI's strength lies in its model-agnostic design, allowing flexible model switching and testing without vendor lock-in. Key Technical Focus: Model Routing and Fault Tolerance: Backend.AI Continuum automatically switches to local resources during cloud outages. The Continuum Router dynamically routes between external APIs, local LLMs, and internal models, stabilizing performance while reducing costs through real-time input/output verification and caching. Infrastructure Bottleneck Evolution: Through participation in the government-backed independent AI foundation model project, Rablup discovered storage I/O—not GPU—represents the primary performance limitation in large-scale infrastructure. They've deployed GPU Direct Storage virtualization to address this. As AI agents emerge, CPU value resurfaces; agents require CPU resources for code modifications and file operations beyond model inference. Ecosystem Strategy: Rablup views neocloud and GPU subscription providers as partners rather than competitors. The company open-sourced MLXcel, a Rust-optimized inference engine for Apple MacBooks, and plans integrating Backend.AI Go for local small language models with server offerings and emerging NPU orchestration.
main.keep_reason: Korean infra startup: storage I/O (not GPU) is the bottleneck in large-scale AI infra, GPU Direct Storage virtualization, heterogeneous GPU+NPU orchestration — directly DPU-adjacent value prop.
main.select_reason: 스토리지 I/O가 대규모 AI 인프라의 실질 병목이라는 진단 + GPU Direct Storage 가상화 + 이종 GPU/NPU 오케스트레이션 — MangoBoost DPU 가치 제안과 거의 1:1 매핑되는 한국 인프라 스타트업 인사이트.

main.title: Elon Musk gets FTC nod to acquire data center optics business Mesh Optical
main.body: The Federal Trade Commission has approved Elon Musk's acquisition of Mesh Optical Technologies, a data center optical networking company established by former SpaceX engineers. The company specializes in optical transceivers designed for artificial intelligence data centers. Mesh Optical's Alpha C1 transceiver supports 1.6T and 800G speeds while claiming to use a third of the power utilization of rival modules. The company secured $50 million in Series A funding in February 2026. The FTC approval specifically names Elon Musk as the acquiring entity rather than SpaceXAI, though Musk frequently blurs boundaries between his various business ventures through cross-selling and staff transfers. Co-founders Travis Brashears, Cameron Ramos, and Serena Grown-Haeberli previously developed optical communication systems for SpaceX's Starlink satellite network. SpaceX recently completed the largest IPO in history and intends to deploy up to one million data center satellites. The company's xAI subsidiary operates terrestrial data centers and has leased capacity to Anthropic, Google, and Reflection. SpaceX also plans a chip manufacturing partnership with Tesla called TeraFab.
main.keep_reason: Musk acquires 1.6T/800G optical transceiver vendor (1/3 power vs rivals) for AI DC — datacenter networking M&A directly in DPU/SmartNIC adjacency.
main.select_reason: 1.6T/800G optical transceiver 벤더 인수 (전력 1/3) — AI DC 네트워킹 M&A로 DPU/SmartNIC 인접 영역, xAI/SpaceX 인프라 수직통합 시그널.

main.title: 딥시크, 오픈소스 추론 최적화 프레임워크 'DSpark' 공개…V4 속도 60~85% 향상
main.body: DeepSeek unveiled DSpark, an open-source speculative decoding framework that achieves 60-85% per-user generation speedup on DeepSeek-V4 models while maintaining 100% output consistency. The framework uses confidence-scheduled speculative decoding with semi-autoregressive generation (CSSD-SAG). Rather than introducing a new model, DSpark is a serving optimization that attaches a draft module to existing DeepSeek-V4 weights. The system works by having a draft model propose token blocks while the full target model verifies them in single forward passes—rejection sampling preserves output distribution exactly, ensuring lossless quality. DSpark combines a parallel draft backbone with a lightweight sequential head to reduce suffix decay during token generation. A confidence-scoring mechanism and load-aware scheduler adapt verification depth based on GPU availability. Benchmarking shows accepted token length increased 26-31% compared to Eagle3 and 16-18% versus DFlash. Production deployments achieved per-user generation running 60-85% faster than the MTP-1 baseline. DeepSeek simultaneously released DeepSpec, an MIT-licensed toolkit for training and evaluating speculative decoding drafters. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-DSpark and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark checkpoints are available via Hugging Face. The release is significant for AI inference infrastructure: it demonstrates that serving-layer optimizations can dramatically reduce hardware costs without model retraining, a key consideration for operators running large-scale inference clusters.
main.keep_reason: DSpark serving-layer optimization: 60-85% per-user speedup without model retraining, GPU-load-aware scheduling — directly addresses MangoBoost's AI inference cost/efficiency value prop.
main.select_reason: 모델 재학습 없이 서빙 계층에서 60-85% 추론 가속 + GPU 부하 인지 스케줄러 — 대규모 추론 클러스터 운영자 관점에서 하드웨어 비용 절감, MangoBoost 추론 가치 제안과 정렬.

main.title: Taking an Up-Close Look at the Supermicro GB300 Super AI Station
main.body: With NVIDIA announcing new desktop system designs at Computex 2026, the company's partners showcased their offerings. The highlight for many was seeing an NVIDIA DGX Station system, priced around $125,000—among the most expensive desktop computers available and the primary way to obtain NVIDIA's GB300 accelerator in a non-server form factor. Supermicro displayed their Super AI Station at Computex, featuring a plexiglass panel allowing attendees to view the interior. NVIDIA maintains strict control over DGX Station designs, providing critical components like the motherboard and processors while allowing OEMs flexibility in overall system design within specified parameters. The system centers on the Grace Blackwell GB300 chip, combining a 72-core Grace CPU with a Blackwell GPU. The 1600-watt TDP necessitates liquid cooling across critical components. Memory comprises four LPDDR5X SOCAMMs delivering 496GB capacity for the CPU, while the GPU uses a de-rated configuration with 7 of 8 HBM3e stacks enabled, yielding 252GB GPU memory and 7.1TB/second bandwidth. Storage includes four PCIe Gen5 x4 M.2 2280 slots. Supermicro's showcase system featured 480GB Micron 7450 Gen4 x4 drives and an NVIDIA RTX PRO video card—necessary since the GB300 lacks graphics capabilities. The system includes dual 400GbE QSFP ports via NVIDIA ConnectX-8 technology. The front-to-back airflow design suits both desktop and rackmount configurations, offering a 5U server mounting option. The DGX Station serves developers and testers needing GB300 access in a desktop environment. Windows versions will become available later in 2026.
main.keep_reason: GB300 desktop spec deep-dive: Grace+Blackwell, 252GB HBM3e, 7.1TB/s, dual 400GbE ConnectX-8 — networking detail directly relevant to DPU/SmartNIC competitive landscape.
main.select_reason: GB300 252GB HBM3e/7.1TB/s + dual 400GbE ConnectX-8 듀얼 포트 — NVIDIA의 데스크톱급 AI 시스템 사양이 DPU/SmartNIC 경쟁 구도(특히 ConnectX-8)와 직접 충돌, 카테고리 분산상 product slot 확보.

competitor_articles.title: 엔비디아, 'GLM-5.2' 4비트 양자화 모델 공개..."정확도 유지·용량 70%↓"
competitor_articles.body: Nvidia has released an optimized checkpoint of Zhipu AI's popular open-source large language model GLM-5.2 using its proprietary NVFP4 (4-bit) quantization technology. The company unveiled "GLM-5.2 NVFP4" via Hugging Face on June 26, enabling both commercial and non-commercial use. This represents Nvidia's Model Optimizer applied to the original GLM-5.2. GLM-5.2 is a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with 753 billion parameters. It supports up to 1 million token context windows through sparse attention and IndexShare indexing, demonstrating inference and coding performance comparable to leading American models. The most significant achievement is compression efficiency. The original FP8-based GLM-5.2 checkpoint measured 1.5 terabytes; NVFP4 quantization reduced this to approximately 410 gigabytes—a ~73% reduction—while maintaining performance with minimal accuracy loss. Unlike traditional 4-bit quantization approaches that sacrifice accuracy, NVFP4 applies variable scales across smaller units and preserves higher precision for accuracy-sensitive layers. Benchmark results showed near-identical performance: GPQA Diamond scores of 89.52 (original) versus 89.39 (NVFP4); some tests showed NVFP4 exceeding baseline performance. However, developers noted contextual limitations: while NVFP4 reduced GPU HBM memory usage by ~300GB and expanded KV cache capacity by 57%, single-stream decoding speed decreased approximately 24% due to lack of Multi-Token Prediction support—making FP8 preferable for high-throughput inference scenarios.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: NVIDIA NVFP4 quantization on 753B-param MoE: 1.5TB→410GB (-73%), HBM -300GB, KV cache +57% — direct AI inference infra cost/memory math relevant to DPU/serving stack.

competitor_articles.title: K-AI Alliance Expands to 50 Members, Elevated to SK's Global AI Platform
competitor_articles.body: SK's AI Committee announced that the K-AI Alliance held its annual Unite 2026 gathering in Menlo Park, Silicon Valley on Wednesday. Approximately 60 attendees participated, including SK leadership and representatives from member companies like Moloco, Bespin Global, Rebellions, and Imprimed, alongside global venture capital and major tech officials. The K-AI Alliance, originally launched in February 2023 by SK Telecom with seven founding members, now comprises 50 companies spanning AI semiconductors, infrastructure, models, and applications. This year, operational responsibility transitioned from SK Telecom to the SK Group's AI Committee, positioning it as a group-level cooperation platform. At Unite 2026, the alliance unveiled K-AI Alliance 2.0, a mid-to-long-term strategy emphasizing joint technology development, proof-of-concept projects, and global customer acquisition. The organization intends to expand regional programs across Japan, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia. SK AI Committee Chairman Yoo Young-sang stated: genuine innovation becomes possible only when the AI full-stack ecosystem is organically connected. He added that the alliance aims to develop into a global AI ecosystem platform that investors and big tech seek out first.
competitor_articles.keep_reason: K-AI Alliance 2.0 launched at Menlo Park Unite 2026 with 50 members including Tier-1 competitor Rebellions; SK Group elevation, global expansion (Japan/ME/SEA) — sovereign AI consortium signal.
